lyrics:
[Intro: solo piano, whistled phrase, slow kick]

[Chorus: high male voice, sung, clean]
There's a new name on the mailbox
The man you want don't live here now
He left one night with what he did
I couldn't tell you where or how
New name on the mailbox
Different man inside the house

[Verse 1: Southern male rap, slow and heavy]
Old partner pulled up in a rental, tinted
Said, "I got a thing, one night, come get it"
I said, "You got the wrong address, my friend
Fella you remember met his end"
Not in a box, not on the news
In a visiting room with his little girl's shoes
Too small for her now, on the table, in a bag
That's the night he died. I ain't seen him since. Don't ask.

[Chorus: high male voice, sung, clean]
There's a new name on the mailbox
The man you want don't live here now
He left one night with what he did
I couldn't tell you where or how
New name on the mailbox
Different man inside the house

[Verse 2: rap, steadier, strings under]
I coach on Saturdays, I'm early every time
I say "yes ma'am" to a boss half my age, that's fine
Parole's done. I still call in. That's just me.
I like somebody knowing where I'll be
The old me's got some friends who want him back
They can't have him. He don't get to see my kids. That's that.
I keep his picture so I don't forget his face
I don't hate him. He just can't come in this place.

[Bridge: piano and whistle, voice low]
If he knocks, I don't answer
If he knocks, I'm not home

[Final Chorus: high voice, choir behind, drums fuller]
There's a new name on the mailbox
The man you want don't live here now
He left one night with what he did
I couldn't tell you where or how
New name on the mailbox
Different man inside the house

[Outro: piano, a mailbox lid, a child calling "Dad!"]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 68 BPM with double-time hi-hats, 4/4, A minor. Slow, wide and solemn, with a pop-sized chorus.

VOICE: The rapper is a man with a deep Georgia drawl, slow and deliberate, almost conversational. The chorus is sung by a different man in a high, clean, pop tenor, doubled, with a choir behind in the last chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: A sad piano figure, a whistled counter-melody, a deep 808 kick and bass, crisp hi-hats, a snare with a long tail, a string section from verse 2, a choir, an acoustic guitar.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano and whistle. 0:16 Chorus 1. 0:50 Verse 1. 1:36 Chorus 2. 2:10 Verse 2. 2:56 Bridge. 3:12 Final chorus. 3:44 Outro, a mailbox and a child's voice at 3:56.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-2000s Atlanta pop-rap: glossy, wide and clean, piano and vocal up front, low end deep.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'I don't hate him. He just can't come in this place.' at 2:50.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original declares the change at the moment it happens. This is fifteen years later, when the hard part is no longer changing but keeping the door shut.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Tested, firm, settled, home.
